newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian scientists announce HIV trial on twins.
newsitem.headline: Australian scientists announce HIV trial on twins.

text.p: Australian scientists on Monday announced a clinical trial in which HIV-positive patients will receive genetically modified cells from their healthy identical twins in the hope that the altered cells will attack the HIV virus.

The scientists said the 12-month trial, involving a group of identical twins in Sydney and Los Angeles, would test whether the modified white blood cells boost the immune system by inhibiting the replication of affected cells.
The trial, starting at Sydney's St Vincent's Hospital, will use a genetic process known as "gene shears" to alter T-cells, the key immune system fighters, to make them anti-HIV in nature.
"The human trials will determine the safety and ability of gene shears in destroying HIV in infected patients," said Federal Science Minister Peter McGauran.
"It may prove to be as important a discovery as that of penicillin," McGauran said in a statement.
